claim_limit: This record preserves a published Gazepoint GP3 data-quality validation study as a native-device evidence lead. The study reports GP3 sampling behavior and evaluates target-fixation detection in a visual-search task, but fixation events were generated algorithmically with the R saccades package and the behavioral reference for target observation was a mouse click. It therefore does not provide independent manual/expert sample-wise fixation/saccade labels and is not eligible as GazeForge native event-classifier ground truth or Frozen Evidence.
dataset: Brand et al. Gazepoint GP3 independent-use validation study
fingerprint_method: SHA-256 of canonical UTF-8 JSON for this object with evidence_fingerprint_sha256 omitted, sort_keys=true and separators=(',', ':').
next_authoritative_gate: Obtain any study dataset or supplementary files from the corresponding author or another authorized source and fingerprint the received bytes.
If raw timestamps are obtained, verify the collection-specific cadence directly from recorded samples rather than treating the nominal GP3 rate as exact.
Do not reuse mouse-click target observation as a sample-wise fixation/saccade event reference.
Continue the search for a real GP3 corpus with independent human/expert event annotations, including fixation and saccade labels plus annotation/adjudication provenance.
Only such independently annotated event data may advance the empirical native event-classifier benchmark.

source.title: Evaluating the data quality of the Gazepoint GP3 low-cost eye tracker when used independently by study participants
